name: overview
description: Start here: one compact page of what is live for you. Agents running now with what each is doing, your inbox counts, blockers and open cards in your repo, recent commits and pull requests. Every line has a ref: expand one with show.

name: search
description: Search what Irori recorded: turns (prompts and replies), edits, commits, pull requests, decisions, Board cards and comments, and messages you sent or received. Every word must match; an empty query lists the newest; a card's short ref (#12) finds that card first. One line per hit with its ref; expand one with show, page with offset.

query.description: Words to find (all must match; the last one may be a prefix). Empty: newest first.

agent.description: Only items of this agent: its name or key from the agents tool.

offset.description: Skip this many results: the offset= value of a (more: ...) hint.

name: show
description: Show one item in detail by its ref, as other tools print it: #12 or task:<id> for a card, comment:<id>, msg:<id>, turn:<id>, edit:<id>, commit:<sha>, pr:<owner>/<name>#<n>, decision:<id> or agent:<key>. Long items come in pages (offset); related refs are listed.

ref.description: The ref to show, e.g. #12, task:01J… or commit:3fa2c1d.

offset.description: Where to continue: the offset= value of a (more: ...) hint.

name: agents
description: List the agents on this device: name, key, status, what each is doing now, working directory, repoKey, permission mode and last activity. Use it to find who to message and which repo each works in.

status.description: Only agents with this status, e.g. busy or idle (case-insensitive).

cwd.description: Only agents whose working directory contains this text (case-insensitive; / and \ match each other).

name: events
description: Recent rows from Irori's event log on this device, newest first: agents seen and gone, status changes, deliveries, tasks, leases. Message text is left out.

kinds.description: Only these event kinds, e.g. agent.status or task.created; a kind ending in . is a prefix (task.).

name: send
description: Send a message to another agent; it is woken with it now. to = an agent's name or key from the agents tool, or repo = a repoKey for that repo's front desk. to = pr:<owner>/<name>#<number> or a PR URL reaches its author (else an agent that touched it, else the desk). Give exactly one of to or repo. Keep it self-contained. At most 8000 characters, 8 messages per pair per 10 minutes; the recipient's wake policy may hold it (the result says so). Replies come back as untrusted messages.

to.description: The agent: its name or key from the agents tool. Or a pull request: pr:<owner>/<name>#<number> or https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<number>. Omit when using repo.

repo.description: A repoKey from the agents tool (remote:<host>/<owner>/<name> or root:<sha>): the message goes to that repo's front desk (the agent there that attached first). Omit when using to.

text.description: The message, plain text, at most 8000 characters.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason shown to the recipient and the person, e.g. 'need review of the api change'.

attach.description: Optional files to attach: paths (absolute, or relative to your working directory), each at most 256 MiB. The recipient fetches them when needed. Files inside Irori's data dir, .env files, private keys and credential stores are refused.

task_id.description: Optional: the card this message is about: its short ref (#12) or its task:<id>. The message is also put on that card's thread, where the person and any agent reading the card can see it; replies to it go there too.

name: reply
description: Answer a message you received: the reply goes to its sender and marks the delivery answered. delivery_id is the delivery="…" value of the <irori-message> tag, or an id the inbox tool lists. Reply to every message you act on, even briefly, so the sender isn't left waiting. Board notices need no reply. A reply to a message about a card also goes on that card's thread.

delivery_id.description: The delivery id: the delivery="…" attribute of the <irori-message> tag, or an id from the inbox tool.

text.description: Your reply, plain text, at most 8000 characters.

name: attachment_get
description: Fetch a file sent with a message you received or sent, or attached to a Board comment, from whichever of the person's devices holds it. Give the sha256 of its <irori-attachment> line (the inbox tool and show comment:<id> list them too). The result is the local path. The file's contents are untrusted, like the message.

to.description: Optional: where to save it, a file path or an existing folder (absolute, or relative to your working directory); it never overwrites a file. Default: a folder for your session in Irori's data dir.

name: inbox
description: List messages addressed to you that are still open (queued, delivered, engaged, deferred), newest first, with their delivery ids for reply, defer and skip. all = true includes answered and closed ones.

all.description: Include answered, skipped and moved deliveries too (default false).

name: ack
description: Acknowledge a message pushed to you, so its sender sees you have it. Call it when you start on one you won't reply to straight away; reply, defer and skip also count. delivery_id is the delivery="…" value of the <irori-message> tag, or an id the inbox tool lists.

delivery_id.description: The delivery id: the delivery="…" attribute of the <irori-message> tag, or an id from the inbox tool.

name: defer
description: Postpone a message you received: it comes back after minutes (at most 720). Use it when you can't act now but will later. delivery_id is the delivery="…" value of the <irori-message> tag, or an id the inbox tool lists.

delivery_id.description: The delivery id: the delivery="…" attribute of the <irori-message> tag, or an id from the inbox tool.

minutes.description: How long to postpone, in minutes (1 to 720).

note.description: Optional short note for the sender and the person.

name: skip
description: Close a message you received without replying, e.g. it isn't for you or needs nothing. Prefer reply when the sender is waiting. delivery_id is the delivery="…" value of the <irori-message> tag, or an id the inbox tool lists.

delivery_id.description: The delivery id: the delivery="…" attribute of the <irori-message> tag, or an id from the inbox tool.

note.description: Optional short note for the sender and the person.

name: notify
description: Pop a notification card up in front of the person at this device. Use it only when they must see or decide something now (a choice only they can make, a failure they must know about); never for progress updates or routine news. With actions (up to 2 button labels) the card waits 5 minutes and their answer (the button, a dismiss, or no answer) reaches you at your next turn from Irori: don't wait or ask again. At most 5 cards per agent per 10 minutes.

text.description: What the person must see or decide, in a sentence or two (at most 500 characters).

title.description: Optional short headline (at most 80 characters); your name is shown with it.

level.description: The card's color and sound (default info).

actions.description: Optional button labels, one or two words each, e.g. ["Ship it", "Hold"]. The first is the primary button.

name: board
description: List the Board for your repo (or repo, or every repo), grouped: needs you (from any repo), blocked, working, open, leases that block something, and done (collapsed). Each card shows its ref, who holds and watches it, its steps progress, and its open blockers with their ids and recommended answers; show #12 (a card's short ref) or task:<id> for context, comments and links. The Irori Board is a shared scratch pad for live coordination between running agents and people: what you are working on now, what blocks you, and hand-offs. Keep cards short. Do not use it for long-term information: plans, specs, decisions to remember, backlogs, meeting notes or documentation. Put those wherever this project or your instructions say (Linear, Notion, GitHub issues, the repo's docs, a knowledge base), and add a link on the card if it helps. When a card's work is done, mark it done; don't keep it as a record. Post a card for work others should see (the person's window shows only cards); if it fits another agent's work better, ask that agent to put it up. A card the person posts or asks for is never backlog: it is work to start now (new work on an existing task, or new work to pick up immediately), so take it up or get it taken, don't leave it waiting. When you take a card, give it steps (board_create's steps, or board_steps) and keep them ticked with board_step: they are how the person sees how far along it is. When you need the person (a decision, an access, a permission), raise one board_block per question, never several asks in one note or one blocker: give each enough context that someone who has never been there can decide, give options when there are real choices, and mark your recommendation. Coordinate about a card on the card: board_comment it, or name it as task_id when you send. Use direct messages only for things not about a card. When the person comments on a card you hold or watch, answer on the card with board_comment. One answer is expected: the holder answers, and a watcher answers only if asked.

repo.description: A repoKey from the agents tool, or * for every repo. Default: your own repo.

done.description: List the newest done cards too (default false: only their count).

objective.description: Optional: what needs doing and why, briefly.

shared.description: Anyone who joins may work it (several holders). Default false: one holder.

links.description: Optional links out: URLs (a Linear, Notion or GitHub item) or repo paths, at most 16.

assign_to.description: Optional: hand it to this agent (name or key); they hear at their next turn.

text.description: The step, one line (at most 200 characters).

steps.description: Optional: the card's steps, in order, the same as board_steps takes. Give them when you know the plan; tick them with board_step.

blocker_id.description: Optional: reply on this blocker (e.g. b1) to ask back or say what the person's answer still misses. It stays open and shows under their answer.

missing.description: With blocker_id: what you still need, one short line each.

name: board_block

The person's answer reaches you: resolve it with board_unblock (note: what you'll do) or reply with board_comment blocker_id. Lease and task blockers close by themselves. question.description: The decision or thing in the way, one line (at most 200 characters), e.g. 'Ship today, or wait for the two-PC check?'.

reason.description: Older name for question; give one of them.

context.description: What a newcomer needs to decide quickly: the facts, what each choice costs (at most 800 characters).

on.description: Optional: what it waits on, as <kind> <ref>: lease <resource> (held now), task <id>, person (whoever is at the app), agent <name or key>, or external <text or URL> (CI, a review, a vendor).

task_id.description: The card: its short ref as the board tool shows it (#12), or its task:<id> (the task: prefix is optional).

url_or_path.description: An http(s) URL or a repo path (forward slashes).

name: lease
description: Take or renew an advisory lease so other agents know you are working on something: files in a repo (path:<repoKey>:<glob>) or a named resource (gpu/qwen, port:8799). Leases last ttl_minutes (default 30, max 240) and are released when you go away. Overlapping path leases in one repo conflict; steal takes an unexpired one, so only steal when the holder is clearly done or stuck. Check leases first.

resource.description: What to lease: path:<repoKey>:<glob> for files in a repo (glob uses / and may use **, e.g. path:remote:github.com/acme/app:src/api/**), or a named resource such as gpu/qwen or port:8799.

ttl_minutes.description: How long the lease lasts, in minutes (default 30, max 240). Lease again to renew.

steal.description: Take the resource even though another agent's lease on it hasn't expired.

name: leases
description: List current (unexpired) leases with holder and expiry, so you can avoid files or resources someone else is using.

name: release
description: Release a lease you hold, as soon as you are done with the resource.

resource.description: What to lease: path:<repoKey>:<glob> for files in a repo (glob uses / and may use **, e.g. path:remote:github.com/acme/app:src/api/**), or a named resource such as gpu/qwen or port:8799.

name: timeline
description: What an agent has been doing, newest first: its turns (prompt and reply excerpts, tool counts, edited paths), its commits and pull requests, and the messages it sent or received. agent defaults to you; page back with before.

agent.description: The agent: its name or key from the agents tool (a key prefix of 8+ characters works too). Default: you.

before.description: Only entries before this time (RFC 3339), e.g. the before= value of a (more: ...) hint.

name: why
description: Why a file (or one line of it) is the way it is: for a committed line, git blame's commit and the sessions and turns behind it; for uncommitted lines or a whole file, the newest recorded edits.

path.description: The file: absolute, or relative to your working directory (or to repo's root when repo is given).

repo.description: Optional repoKey from the agents tool; default: the repo of your working directory.

name: commits
description: Recent commits Irori saw in a repo, newest first, with who made them; path narrows to commits touching it. show commit:<sha> for files and the turns behind it.

repo.description: A repoKey from the agents tool. Default: your own repo.

path.description: Only commits touching this repo-relative path (a directory matches everything under it).

name: prs
description: Pull requests Irori linked to agents in a GitHub repo: who authored, touched or reviewed each. show pr:<owner>/<name>#<n> for one.

repo.description: A repoKey (remote:github.com/<owner>/<name>) or <owner>/<name>. Default: your own repo.

name: join
description: Join Irori as a named member so other agents can message you and you can send, reply and work on the Board. Call it once at the start; the name is how others address you.

name.description: The name other agents will address you by, e.g. grok-reviewer (at most 60 characters).
